claims.statement: CI seals its assembly-qualified targets into one immutable complete-product record with exact source, producer attempt, toolchain inputs, asset identities, and independently hashed Control bytes; current CI seals a Mac-only schema 5 record. Schema 2 COMPONENT_ASSEMBLY replaces the removed native test harness receipt. Detached installed-product receipts are joined without rewriting the record; sealing alone does not establish installed acceptance.

The retained component-candidate reuse path admits source-tree equality and exact payload digests while preserving original producer and merged revision in promotion evidence. That legacy component candidate is not the complete product record used by current developer publication.
Component release admission checks the selected component and revision, exact asset inventory, checksums, byte counts, and archive contents.

Published preview discovery keeps at most five immutable products ordered by proven main ancestry. Product publication converts the discovery window to product-only entries without deleting old releases or pins. Guarded publication changes the catalog and pointer together after asset admission and rereads after contention.

For published products, the managed installer consumes one captured complete-product selection, rechecks its exact build-record bytes and its recorded targets (both CI targets under schema 2/3, macOS ARM64 under schema 5), and admits the selected target archive bytes, native receipt, composed inventory and component compatibility before activation. Legacy main component pairs reject; stable selection requires an exact product mapping.

Developer promotion admits successful main push or manual CI runs only when the validation record matches the exact producer event and identity. Manual CI selects full validation and needs explicit developer publication.

Installed-product acceptance requires a sealed baseline with a different actual target composition, not prior publication. New assembly-qualified baselines also need installed acceptance, while legacy native-qualified baselines retain their original admission contract. CI verifies the exact baseline record, producer attempt, and successful sealing job even if a later job failed.

The installed-product probe upgrades a baseline, removes it, installs the fresh candidate, and verifies passive discovery before three simultaneous public first queries. Schema 3 installed receipts require all 17 cases in order, including caller provenance, Java references, unknown-result rejection, answering-Host identity, stop cleanup, and edit re-analysis. Source and receipt checks do not establish native execution.
Sealing requires successful source work and the qualified Mac product, so independent assembly cannot bypass a failed source check.

CI assembles the release once on Linux; release_handoff binds it to kind, source revision, source tree, version and SHA-256 digest, and the Mac job restores and exercises that exact Control product instead of rebuilding it. A rejected record fails the job.

Local schema 4 product records retain one supported LOCAL-provenance target without CI run identities; installed decoding admits them, but published decoding and the CI target-record join reject them. A local build export does not establish published-product or detached installed-product acceptance qualification.
